info.title: compliance
info.description:
Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) is an indirect method of collecting Income Tax. TDS is based on the principle of “Pay as you earn” which is beneficial for both the Government and the taxpayer. It is where a person making a payment of specified nature is liable to deduct tax at a prescribed rate. This ensures continuous revenue for the Government by way of Tax Deducted at the Source.

The Payer making a payment is also responsible to deposit TDS with the Income Tax Department within a specified date and file a TDS Return. Once filed, the deposited amount will be shown in the Payee's Form 26AS which they can then use to claim tax credits when filing ITR.

However, staying TDS compliant can be a hassle for businesses, as they are required to :

1. Deduct TDS from payments that are liable for TDS Deduction at an appropriate rate.
    
2. Deposit TDS to Government before the due date.
    
3. File TDS Returns on a Quarterly basis.
    
4. Issue a TDS Certificate by the deductor to the deductee.
    

Organizations deducting TDS have to remain compliant with each of the steps. Failure to do so results in TDS Penalties by Authorities. Sandbox provides TDS Compliance APIs to help you automate end-to-end TDS compliance.

post.description:
Retrieves a TDS challan and its tax and available consumption details from TRACES.

Identify the challan using the deductor's TAN, BSR code, deposit date, and challan serial number. The deposit date uses epoch milliseconds and the Asia/Kolkata calendar date.

Requires registered TRACES deductor credentials for the requested TAN and Sandbox authentication.

Returns HTTP 521 when no challan matches the supplied particulars. A null consumption_details value means utilization details are unavailable; it does not indicate an unused challan.

post.description:
Searches a deductor's TDS challans by deposit-date range and returns one page of results from TRACES.

Provide the deductor's TAN, from_date_epoch, and to_date_epoch. Both dates are required and use epoch milliseconds. The calendar dates are interpreted in Asia/Kolkata.

page_number starts at 0. page_size specifies the number of challans requested per page. Both fields are optional.

The response includes the challans in data and the pagination totals totalPages and totalElements. A page with no challans returns HTTP 200 with an empty data list.

Requires registered TRACES deductor credentials for the requested TAN and Sandbox authentication.

get.summary: Get bulk PAN verification job status
get.description:
Returns the current status of a bulk PAN verification job in your workspace. This GET request has no body.

A created job waits for the workbook upload. queued waits to start processing. in_progress covers workbook validation, TRACES authentication and verification, and output workbook generation. A job succeeds after the output JSON workbook is saved and provides output_json_url for its download. A failed job provides message. Retrieving a failed job returns HTTP 200.

TRACES report availability is polled for up to one day after successful submission. Authentication, validation, processing, and report-availability failures appear on the job.

The output workbook contains payee_sheet and payee_table with the header ["sr_no", "pan", "pan_status"]. It includes only submitted PANs returned by TRACES, in their original input order. The first input sr_no is retained for each PAN. A missing PAN is omitted and does not fail the job.

The pan_status value is the exact text returned by TRACES. Known values include Valid and Operative, Valid and Inoperative, Valid, Inactive, and Invalid. Other source values are returned unchanged. An Invalid PAN result does not mean the job failed. The input file limit does not limit the output file.

Output workbook example:

```json
{
  "@entity": "workbook",
  "name": "pan_verification_workbook",
  "sheets": [
    {
      "@entity": "sheet",
      "name": "payee_sheet",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "@entity": "table",
          "name": "payee_table",
          "header": [
            "sr_no",
            "pan",
            "pan_status"
          ],
          "rows": [
            [
              1,
              "ABCPD1234E",
              "Valid and Operative"
            ],
            [
              2,
              "XYZPK5678L",
              "Valid and Inoperative"
            ]
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

This example omits the repeated input PAN and a PAN absent from the TRACES report.
